title: Word-of-mouth dances and fights in Kansas City
summary: He marvels at how crowds of a thousand gathered by word of mouth for bands, with fights over musicians.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: But the thing that I could never understand, Dan, is how in the hell that on weekends everybody'd go out and go into a club and the place'd be crowded and by word of mouth and, you know, and you'd have hundreds of people gathering and you'd have picnics and you didn't have...you couldn't put it in The Daily News, The Post wasn't available, The Village Voice wasn't available, the local papers printed once the week for blacks, and by the time that that came out on Friday or Saturday...but it was amazing how, that by word of mouth, these could become so famous, and so popular. And people people would know they're coming to town, and they would crowd out the dance halls. Well, when I say crowd out, you take a thousand people...a lot of people. And they'd have a dance hall with a thousand people in the place.

And fights galore, you know what I mean, and people fighting over the musicians and...and another segment of the people really loved them, really appreciated them and...I guess that's just the way society is structured. You're going to have these problems wherever you go.
